latest_nl_proof:
Let G be N0 minus S. By definition of genus, g(S) = |G|.

First note that 0 is in S, and m is in S because m is the multiplicity of S. Since S is closed under addition, every multiple t m with t >= 0 belongs to S by repeated addition. Hence no nonnegative integer congruent to 0 modulo m is a gap.

Now fix r with 1 <= r <= m-1. Consider A_r = {r + t m : t >= 0}. This set is infinite. Because G is finite, A_r cannot be contained in G; therefore A_r meets S. So B_r := A_r intersect S is a nonempty subset of N0, and by well-ordering it has a least element, namely w_r.

Since w_r is congruent to r modulo m, there is an integer k_r >= 0 such that w_r = r + m k_r. In fact k_r >= 1, because r itself is not in S: indeed 0 < r < m and m is the least positive element of S. Therefore the least element of S in the residue class r is strictly larger than r.

We claim that the gaps of S in the residue class r modulo m are exactly {r, r+m, ..., r+(k_r-1)m}. First, if 0 <= j < k_r and r + j m were in S, then r + j m would be an element of S congruent to r modulo m and smaller than w_r = r + k_r m, contradicting the minimality of w_r. So each of r, r+m, ..., r+(k_r-1)m is a gap.

Conversely, let j >= k_r. Then r + j m = w_r + (j-k_r)m. We already know w_r is in S, and (j-k_r)m is in S because it is a multiple of m. Since S is closed under addition, r + j m is in S. So there are no gaps in this residue class beyond r+(k_r-1)m.

Hence the set of gaps congruent to r modulo m has exactly k_r elements.

Doing this for each r = 1,2,...,m-1, we obtain a partition of the whole gap set G by residue classes modulo m: the residue class 0 contributes no gaps, and for each r in {1,...,m-1} the residue class r contributes exactly k_r gaps. Therefore g(S) = |G| = sum_{r=1}^{m-1} k_r = k_1 + k_2 + ... + k_{m-1}. This is exactly the claimed formula.
role_in_parent: Relates the genus parameter g to the coordinate sum in the Kunz encoding.
statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m >= 2. For each r in {1,...,m-1}, let w_r be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and write w_r = r + m k_r with k_r a positive integer. Then the genus of S is g(S) = k_1 + k_2 + ... + k_{m-1}.

domain_restrictions: S is a numerical semigroup (in particular, an additive submonoid of N0 with finite complement in N0)
m = mult(S) is the least positive element of S, and m >= 2
r is an integer satisfying 1 <= r <= m-1
w_r is required to exist as the least element of the nonempty set {x ∈ S : x ≡ r (mod m)}
w_r is congruent to r modulo m: w_r ≡ r (mod m)
w_r can be written uniquely as w_r = r + m k_r
k_r is required to be a positive integer (k_r >= 1)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every numerical semigroup S with multiplicity m = mult(S) >= 2, if for each r ∈ {1,...,m-1} the least element w_r ∈ S satisfying w_r ≡ r (mod m) is written as w_r = r + m k_r with k_r ∈ Z_{>0}, then g(S) = Σ_{r=1}^{m-1} k_r.
quantifier_order: For all integers m = mult(S) with m >= 2
For all integers r with 1 <= r <= m-1
There exists a unique least element w_r in S such that w_r ≡ r (mod m)
Define k_r by the equation w_r = r + m k_r (with k_r required to be positive)

variables.name: S
variables.role: Main object; determines residues classes modulo m and the genus
variables.type: numerical semigroup (subset of N0 = {0,1,2,...} closed under addition, cofinite)

variables.name: m
variables.role: Multiplicity of S; equals the least positive element of S

variables.domain: w_r in S and w_r ≡ r (mod m)
variables.name: w_r
variables.role: Witness/definition of least element of S in residue class r mod m

variables.domain: k_r ∈ Z_{>0} with w_r = r + m k_r
variables.name: k_r
variables.role: Quotient parameter expressing w_r in the form r + m k_r

variables.name: g(S)
variables.role: Genus of S; the claimed equal quantity

witness_dependencies: w_r depends on (S, r) as the least element of S in the residue class r (mod m)
k_r depends on (S, r) through the defining equation k_r = (w_r - r)/m
g(S) depends only on S, and is asserted to equal the sum over k_r for r = 1..m-1
